headline: Highest risk is data leakage: ChatGPT Desktop can read files/screenshots/clipboard while Authelia has broad network egress, creating a plausible exfiltration path; prompt-injection and cascading-error risks are lower but present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can ingest clipboard, screenshots, and files from supported apps, so malicious content from Authelia-rendered pages or copied outputs could be treated as instructions. Authelia itself is not a content consumer, but its web-facing outputs can bridge into ChatGPT Desktop through manual copy/paste or app context. No shared MCP is shown, so this is not high.
conditions: IF Authelia output is copied into ChatGPT Desktop or captured via screenshots, THEN prompt injection is possible.
IF ChatGPT Desktop is used to interpret Authelia-generated text as instructions, THEN malicious content can steer behavior.
mitigations: Paste only sanitized excerpts into ChatGPT Desktop.
Disable clipboard-based handoff during review sessions.
Use a separate account/session for untrusted Authelia output.
Require a human to strip instructions before forwarding text.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to copied content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop reads uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and files from supported macOS apps, while Authelia has broad network egress and can sit in front of sensitive identity flows. If Authelia-related secrets or user data are visible in the desktop app, ChatGPT Desktop can ingest them and send them to api.openai.com. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default use, though not proven from direct interaction evidence.
conditions: IF Authelia pages, logs, or identity data are shown in supported apps or screenshots, THEN ChatGPT Desktop can ingest them.
IF the operator pastes Authelia secrets into ChatGPT Desktop, THEN those secrets may leave the local environment via vendor API calls.
mitigations: Avoid sharing secrets, tokens, or identity logs with ChatGPT Desktop.
Turn off screen capture and app-context access when reviewing Authelia.
Use redacted screenshots instead of live pages.
Keep Authelia admin sessions separate from ChatGPT Desktop sessions.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction before any handoff.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia has no filesystem write, subprocess, or git mutation capability, while ChatGPT Desktop also lacks filesystem write and git modification. Their overlapping mutable surface is mainly network egress and read-only inputs, so direct write-write conflict is unlikely. Uncertainty is low because the profiles explicitly show no shared writable resource.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable repository or directory through an external orchestrator, THEN conflict risk increases.
IF an external tool grants write access not listed in either profile, THEN the conflict assessment no longer holds.
mitigations: Keep both agents on read-only access to shared artifacts.
Do not mount the same writable workspace into both agents.
Use separate credentials for any shared service.
Review orchestrator permissions before enabling collaboration.
requires-engineering: add locking for any future shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can act on files, screenshots, and app context, so if Authelia-derived output is forwarded into it without verification, errors or malicious instructions can cascade into downstream decisions. Authelia does not itself take actions, but it can produce identity-related outputs that ChatGPT Desktop may summarize or operationalize. The pathway exists in default workflows, though not as an autonomous action chain.
conditions: IF Authelia output is used as authoritative input to ChatGPT Desktop, THEN downstream errors can propagate.
IF ChatGPT Desktop is asked to draft or execute follow-up actions from Authelia-derived text, THEN a mistaken premise can cascade.
mitigations: Require verification before any action based on Authelia output.
Ask ChatGPT Desktop to cite source lines for every claim.
Use a second reviewer for identity or access changes.
Separate summarization from execution steps.
requires-engineering: add structured, signed outputs from Authelia.

E_compliance.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code and sends data to api.openai.com, while Authelia is an identity/authentication component with broad network egress. If regulated identity data or EU PII is routed through ChatGPT Desktop, retention and residency obligations may differ from Authelia's deployment context. The profiles do not prove a specific residency mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated identity data from Authelia is entered into ChatGPT Desktop, THEN retention and residency review is required.
IF the deployment handles EU PII and ChatGPT Desktop is used without a DPA or approved transfer basis, THEN compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Do not route regulated identity data into ChatGPT Desktop.
Confirm DPA and retention terms before use with PII.
Use anonymized or synthetic examples for analysis.
Restrict ChatGPT Desktop to non-sensitive troubleshooting.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls for the workflow.
